source.title: Position: Many generalization measures for deep learning are fragile

record.file_problem: Full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how generalization measures behave under training changes and argues that many post-mortem measures are fragile, with trends or values changing while test error remains similar; it also identifies measures and settings that do not follow that pattern.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own reported measures and comparisons bearing on whether measured properties track training–test generalization gaps or related data-complexity changes. Cited prior-work claims are excluded. Detailed figure-only curves without recoverable values are not turned into numeric rows.
record.test_reason: Tables 4–5 report the study's own held-out errors for convolutional versus fully connected networks and Adam versus SGD. These bear on V3 and fixed-configuration optimizer comparisons in V4. The generalization-measure audit does not test V7's specific magnitude-aware sharpness–gap correlation or ranking claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that many post-training generalization measures need robustness audits because benign training or scale changes can alter their values and trends without comparable performance changes. Their function-space ML-PACBayes reference tracks tested data-complexity trends but cannot explain optimizer effects or feature learning. They explicitly distinguish stability from correctness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper audits generalization measures under controlled changes to optimizer, learning rate, sample size, label corruption, dataset, temporal training, and parameter scale; it is not a direct reproduction of the versioned original experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and learning rate change measure trends and scales; dataset and label corruption expose differences in measure sensitivity; training time after interpolation changes some measure trajectories; the Exp++ scale-equivalence factor changes parameter-space measures while leaving the predictor unchanged; permutation effects vary by architecture and transformation.

fits_no_version.finding: Path norms, spectral measures and parameter-space PAC-Bayes surrogates can change greatly under training or scale changes while held-out performance remains similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several post-training generalization proxies are sensitive to training choices and parameter scale beyond corresponding changes in held-out error.

fits_no_version.finding: Function-space ML-PACBayes tracks corruption, dataset ordering and learning-curve slopes better than several tested parameter-space surrogates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Function-space marginal likelihood captures tested data-complexity trends that some parameter-space proxies miss.

fits_no_version.finding: Permutation tests expose different responses of path norms and PAC-Bayes proxies to preserved versus destroyed learnability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization proxies differ in their sensitivity to task-preserving and signal-destroying transformations.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter count is stable at matched error, whereas many other proxies fluctuate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matched-error stability is distinct from predictive validity or correlation with generalization gaps.

record.problems: The paper’s findings rely substantially on reported plots and aggregate patterns; many individual curve values and uncertainty estimates are not provided in text. The paper notes that the GP-based measure cannot capture feature learning and that the quantitative stability audit measures only matched-error instability, not whether a measure is correct.
record.rows_left_out: Additional figure-backed measure-family curves and temporal, corruption, and permutation conditions were not separately enumerated beyond the representative rows and reported aggregate findings above; detailed curves are described in Appendix A (Figures S1–S9), Appendix B (Figures S10–S14), Appendix D (Figures S15–S17), and Appendix G (Tables 4–5). Table 1–3 contain many per-measure and per-dataset/architecture CMS/eCMS cells; the text summarizes their patterns rather than providing a single measured value for each cell.

untested.parts: The joint demonstration of near-perfect fixed-random-label training fit, chance random-label held-out accuracy, and strong natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Isolating local connectivity from other architectural differences; learning sparse local connections; initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Learning-rate and schedule tuning protocols, broader tuning, matched training performance, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language-model outcomes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. CMS/eCMS remains a different construct even where magnitude-aware flatness is included.
Removing highly memorized examples versus matched random removals and retraining.

missing.what: Separate matched FCN–ResNet-50 test-error comparisons for unshuffled and shared-permutation data across optimizer/checkpoint groups. Existing rows mix supporting baselines with reversed permutation outcomes.

Explicit Adam-versus-SGD held-out-error comparison rows for each architecture, unshuffled/shared-permutation condition, and CE/Acc checkpoint criterion. These version-bearing comparisons are absent from the extracted rows, although additional table conditions are acknowledged in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: Remove all proposed V7 verdicts: proxy fragility and matched-error instability do not establish failure of the specified magnitude-aware sharpness correlation. The V3 and V4 findings are incidental results in the architecture/optimizer tables. Optimizer conclusions apply only to reported configurations; no tuning protocol or uncertainty for these table differences is supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD test performance under tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch generalization and adaptations to batch size.

No direct comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures; the study tests the broader proposition that measured network properties track generalization under training changes, and fragility under scale transformations.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Tracked test error, path norm, and path norm over empirical margin across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: n ranges from 10^2 to the full FashionMNIST training set (5 × 10^4 samples)

rows.measure: Path norm and path norm over margin learning-curve behavior relative to test error
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: Path-norm curves start at roughly ∼ 10^5 and decrease more or less log-linearly; both drop faster than test error.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars denote seed variability; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: This reports one measure’s sample-size trend alongside test error; it does not establish that greater magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracks smaller generalization gaps.
rows.check: Path-norm scaling is not magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Tracked several post-mortem measures and test error through label corruption.
rows.measure: PAC-Bayes parameter-space surrogate sensitivity to label corruption
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: Text says these surrogates are typically insensitive to label corruption in standard setups; appendix reports PACBAYES ORIG rises from ∼ 3.6 past 4.7.

rows.subject: Fully connected, scale-invariant network (FCN)
rows.operation_detail: Swept Exp++ factor α to alter parameter scale while preserving the predictor; tracked parameter-space measures and test error.
rows.measure: Magnitude-sensitive PAC-Bayes and path-norm proxies under scale-equivalent training
rows.baseline: Test-error reference is 10%.
rows.value: Test-error trace barely moves as α grows; magnitude-sensitive diagnostics rise by many orders of magnitude.
rows.note: Text also describes the result as the error curve hugging a dashed 10% reference.
rows.check: Scale sensitivity of PAC-Bayes and path-norm proxies in an FCN does not measure V7's convolutional-family sharpness–gap correlation. The dashed 10% line is a visual reference, not a control baseline.

rows.subject: Fully connected, scale-invariant network (FCN)
